fixture.description: Fixture name identifying the fixture project under fixtures-src/. The first character must be ASCII alphanumeric; the remainder admits the canonical [A-Za-z0-9._@-] set plus a single-byte space and Latin-1 letters (U+00C0-U+00FF) so hostile-path aliases validate; control characters (tab/newline) are rejected by the pattern. HOSTILE ALIAS CONVENTION: a fixture value that is not a canonical fixtures-src/ directory (contains a space or a non-ASCII character) is an alias — bin/tt-fixture-provision.mjs resolves the alias to its canonical fixture for golden-bare and fixture-source lookups while the work clone path keeps the manifest name verbatim (W1.X1: 'tt-ts café' resolves to tt-ts). Alias values are reserved and deliberately authored, never ad-hoc.

seed.description: OPTIONAL immutable seed git ref the working fixture clone should land on. Holds a ref NAME (e.g. 'BUG-P1' or 'seed/storm' or 'broken-tests'), never a 'refs/...' prefix: the provisioning stage resolves a bare name by checking it out directly as given, and resolves a branch-style name (no 'seed/' prefix) onto the working clone's current branch. A seed ref reproduces the case's exact starting tree (green base + exactly one seeded defect) per spec 02-fixture-projects.md green-base + seed-ref discipline. Absent or null => provision from the fixture's green baseline.

harness.description: Harness that executes the case. pi/hermes/dsh are REAL harnesses (dsh is the Tier-2 distributed-shell lane; scripted-dsh does not exist — a dsh case is always real). scripted-pi/scripted-hermes are the zero-token scripted runtimes; local is the contained local-command hook.

test_cmd.description: RAW test command the workflow actually runs in this fixture — passed to the harness as --context test_cmd=<value> and fed into launchGateKey (O2/O9/O10 evidence); never a pre-wrapped shim invocation. Per-fixture canonical commands: tt-python and tt-python@master use .venv/bin/pytest -q; tt-ts uses npm test; tt-poly-lite uses ./run-all-tests. Verify against the fixture/workflow config before authoring — never guess.

replay_of.description: OPTIONAL replay-pair binding (S9 / E3.D). Names the paired probe case id (e.g. W1.REPLAY-python -> W1.L2-python) whose work clone and committed tree this REPLAY case MUST reuse per TSTX's origin-scoped contract (spec 05 cross-cutting 'TSTX cross-run replay': unchanged trees, suites must replay with TAMANDUA-TEST CACHED / ledger row reuse, not re-execute; spec 08 W4.28: ledger rows keyed per origin_repo, zero cross-repo replay). Contract: a replay case MUST reuse its pair's work clone (same origin_repo, same committed tree), MUST be sequenced after the pair reaches terminal, and its outcome MUST assert a shim cache HIT (lookup->cache_hit). The controller must treat replay_of as internal wiring and exclude it from --context passthrough (like execution_mode).

token_saver_control.description: OPTIONAL token-saver paired-launch signal (S12 / E3.D). Marks the case as the token-saver lifecycle probe (W3.23-token-saver): the controller executes it as TWO do-now launches — a flagged run with --no-hurry-please-save-tokens-mode and the managed pi-token-saver stub (bin/tt-token-saver-stub) on the contained daemon's PATH (var/adapters-bin, prepended by tt-daemon-up ensure-up), and a control run without either — and records both runs' argv + token ledgers as case evidence. The controller must treat token_saver_control as internal wiring and exclude it from --context passthrough (like execution_mode).

o9_special_exits.description: OPTIONAL O9 special-exit battery opt-in (internal wiring, like token_saver_control; E3.C US-001 migration). Marks the case for the controller's O9 targeted-probe battery: the RESTORED working tree is the evidence the battery produces (exit-88 tracked-dirty refusal, tracked-byte restoration, junk-probe removal) and the controller keeps the clone on PASS instead of pruning it. Formerly carried as the loose chaos.o9_special_exits carrier; moved to context when chaos became the typed W3.17b injection block — the old carrier is REJECTED by the schema.

requires.description: CANONICAL HOST-ADAPTATION CONTRACT (predicates). Every entry is evaluated against the host capability profile emitted by W0.0 (tt-verify-environment) as host-profile.json. A predicate that the host cannot satisfy gates the case to outcome NOT_RUN (predicate) with evidence — it is never silently skipped and never a failure. See tamandua-torture-test-spec/01-environment-and-isolation.md and oracles/CONTRACT.md (host-adaptation note) for the single authoritative contract; every representation here MUST agree with the profile's real key names or the case drifts.

toolchains.description: CANONICAL CONTRACT: an ARRAY of toolchain names; each name is SATISFIED iff the host profile records `toolchains.<name>.present === true` (a Boolean leaf) using the profile's REAL key names (python3, node, go, rust/cargo, java+maven). buildPassed/testPassed (W0.0's --fast probes leave them null) are NOT required for a predicate to be satisfied. A missing/inactive toolchain gates the case NOT_RUN (predicate) with expected true / observed evidence — never silently skipped.

capabilities.description: CANONICAL CONTRACT: harness capabilities `pi`, `hermes`, and `dsh` map to harness PRESENCE recorded in the host profile (harness.<name>.present Boolean leaf; spec 01 makes pi/hermes operator-preconfigured, and the Tier-2 dsh lane is operator-directed — W0.0 RECORDS mechanical presence for all three, never installs). The host profile ALSO records Boolean-leaf capability names under `capabilities.<name>` — e.g. `node-runtimes-2` (true iff W0.0 discovered >= 2 DISTINCT node runtimes/versions on the host; the W4.23 daemon-cross-runtime predicate source) and `daemon-scripted` (a Boolean leaf COMPUTED ON BOTH linux AND darwin: true iff the host has the scripted-daemon plain-background fallback launch prerequisites — bash AND nohup AND node resolvable via POSIX `command -v` PATH lookup; it is the tier1 W2 scripted cells' narrowest true requirement, replacing their former blanket `platform: linux` predicate — daemon-control's non-systemd fallback launch path makes those cells runnable on a host without systemd user scopes, procfs, or getent). Any other capability name is resolved against the profile per the same Boolean-leaf rule. An honestly-present capability must NOT be gated; an honestly-absent capability gates the case NOT_RUN (predicate) with expected/observed evidence.

probe_sequence.description: OPTIONAL E3.C lifecycle-probe sequence (nullable). A per-run list of probe groups the controller executes against the CONTAINED TT instance (43xx CLI, contained env) while the case's run(s) are in flight. null or absent => no lifecycle probes. Each group targets ONE run ordinal (>= 1; ordinals index the case's runs in launch order, so W3.20's two runs use groups run 1 and run 2) and carries an ordered actions array executed when the group's run reaches the action's phase marker. Every probe action + observed effect is recorded into attempt evidence for O16. Schema contract: op enum is fail-closed (unknown ops are REJECTED), when is a phase-marker string (step:<role>:<state> | event:<type> | now), hold_seconds applies to hold-capable ops (pause, pause_drain, sigstop_sigcont), and expect declares the observed effect the O16 lifecycle oracle must judge.

chaos.description: E3.C typed chaos-injection block (nullable). null => no chaos injection. A non-null block is honored by the controller via bin/tt-chaos: type is the injection kind (sigstop_sigcont | kill-harness | kill-daemon | delete-tstx-row | move-branch), target the affected process/data class (per-type), trigger the phase marker that arms the injection, hold_seconds the SIGSTOP hold duration (sigstop_sigcont only), signal the kill signal (kill actions only, default SIGKILL), tree the TSTX tree hash to delete (delete-tstx-row only), ref/repeat/interval_s/wait_timeout_s/rearm/rearm_hold_s the move-branch target-ref injection params (US-004, US-007 S36), operator the executable that performs the injection. Schema contract is fail-closed: unknown type/target/operator/signal values and unknown properties are REJECTED; per-type target/param constraints are enforced by the controller's semantic validator.

production_duration_floor_ms.description: OPTIONAL per-case duration-floor pin (S43a US-006: the per-cell floor override). When declared, oracle-context emits THIS case's o1_wave duration-floor row with the pinned value and O1 judges the case's run against it (the per-cell floor is AUTHORITATIVE for that cell) instead of the family production-median / w1-median floor. Cells whose honest duration differs from the family median (e.g. W4.08-control's honest run measured 13% under the 600s family floor) declare a per-cell floor to absorb honest variance; the family floor still applies to non-declaring cells (fail-closed default unchanged). The flag form (expected_fast_failure: true) opts a fast-honest cell out of the floor entirely.

production_duration_floor_basis.description: OPTIONAL recalibration basis documenting WHY a production_duration_floor_ms value was chosen (operator decision record, e.g. measured honest baseline durations). Informational only — never consumed by oracles or the controller.

expected_fast_failure.description: OPTIONAL fast-honest cell declaration (S43a US-006). TRUE = this cell's CORRECT behavior is early termination (a refusal / small-do-now / auth-expiry run that honestly finishes well under the family production-median duration floor). O1's duration-floor evaluation must NOT flag such a cell's honest early termination against the family floor: its wave run rows are excluded from BOTH the fast numerator and the eligible denominator of the family rate, and the cell is excluded from w1-median calibration samples (the per-cell flag is authoritative for that cell). The family floor still applies to non-flagged cells (fail-closed default unchanged). FALSE/absent = the cell is floor-judgeable like every other cell. Declared on the tier2 rows whose task text mandates early termination (W4.37, W4.38-hostile-task-real, W4.47, W4.dsh-do-now); production floors are kept for cells that must not be fast (e.g. W4.08-control, which instead declares a per-cell production_duration_floor_ms).

arming.description: OPTIONAL S42 (US-005) arming declaration: the case's task/traceability mandates a seed/arm (a reset-hook arming overlay or a seeded arm) that must be PERFORMED before the corridor produces a verdict. A block with mandatory: true makes the controller fail closed as TEST_INFRA_FAIL 'arm-absent' at terminal when the mandated arming was never performed (no per-case arming manifest under var/arming/<case-id>.json, or a manifest recording armed !== true / a type or count that disagrees with the declaration). The reset hook that performs the arming writes that manifest after provably arming. Absent or null => no arming obligation (the S42 gate never fires).

mandatory.description: TRUE = the mandated arming is an obligation: at terminal, the per-case arming manifest must exist and record the declared arming, else TEST_INFRA_FAIL 'arm-absent' (never a vacuous verdict).

type.description: The arming the case mandates (e.g. 'red-baseline' — 2 documented pre-existing red tests planted by the case's reset hook).

count.description: Optional expected arming magnitude (e.g. 2 pre-existing red tests) the manifest must record.

run.description: Run ordinal (1-based) this probe group targets, indexing the case's runs in launch order.

op.description: Probe verb executed by the controller against the contained TT instance. pause: pause the daemon without draining; pause_drain: pause --drain (current run finishes, no new dispatch); resume: resume a paused/failed daemon or run; cancel: cancel the run (assert run.canceled terminal event); fail_force: fail --force the run (resume must reuse the SAME run id); restart_daemon: restart the contained daemon mid-flight (daemon-level MULTI-RUN op — the W3.22 concurrent shape); sigstop_sigcont: SIGSTOP/SIGCONT the harness process; restart_contained_daemon (S44a): restart the CONTAINED daemon mid-run via bin/daemon-control (single-run operator-seam op — the W4.10/W4.48a/W4.33a corridor; NEVER the operator's live 33xx daemon); update_contained_install (S44a): run `tamandua update --force` against the CONTAINED install during a hold (single-run operator-seam op — the W4.33b corridor; the tamandua binary must resolve inside torture-test/var or the action fails closed); invalidate_credentials / restore_credentials (S44a): replace/restore the CONTAINED home's .pi/agent/auth.json with an invalid token (the W4.47 corridor; NEVER the real ~/.pi — a symlink/escaping target is refused).

anyOf.description: Phase marker arming the probe: 'now' (immediate), 'step:<role>:<state>' (e.g. step:developer:running, step:finalize_merge:running), or 'event:<type>' (e.g. event:run.canceled).

AWAITED trigger (S18b): the probe action arms only when the contained run reaches the declared status or the declared event type lands in the contained event stream, bounded by timeout_s. Exactly ONE of status|event is allowed (both at once is rejected). NOTE: the two alternatives are expressed as an anyOf of complete object forms (NOT oneOf) because the controller's bundled schema validator implements anyOf but not oneOf — the per-arm additionalProperties:false makes both-at-once fail BOTH arms, and the per-arm required enforces timeout_s.

status.description: Contained run status to await (product run-status vocabulary — examples: paused, failed, completed, canceled, running).

timeout_s.description: How long (seconds) to await the trigger before the probe fails (probe-trigger-unreached).

event.description: Event type to await in the contained event stream (substring match on the event name — e.g. run.process_cleanup, run.canceled).

timeout_s.description: How long (seconds) to await the trigger before the probe fails (probe-trigger-unreached).

when.description: Phase marker arming the probe: a string marker ('now' | 'step:<role>:<state>' | 'event:<type>') or an awaited object trigger ({"status":"paused","timeout_s":120} awaiting the run status, or {"event":"run.process_cleanup","timeout_s":120} awaiting the event type).

hold_seconds.description: OPTIONAL hold duration for hold-capable ops (pause, pause_drain, sigstop_sigcont): the pause/stop is held this many seconds before the action's counterpart (resume/cont) fires.

during_hold.description: OPTIONAL S44a operator-seam concurrency marker: when true, this action fires CONCURRENTLY with the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING action's hold (the preceding action must carry hold_seconds > 0 — enforced fail-closed by the controller's semantic validator). The operator-seam actions (restart_contained_daemon, update_contained_install) declare it to act DURING a pause hold (W4.33a restarts the contained daemon during the pause hold; W4.33b runs `tamandua update --force` during the hold). Single-run sequences only (rejected on multi-run shapes).

expect.description: OPTIONAL observed-effect declaration the O16 lifecycle oracle judges from the probe evidence.

probeExpect.description: Observed-effect contract for a probe action (all fields optional; O16 judgment dimensions).

run_completes.description: After resume/cont, the probed run must complete.

no_rounds_during_hold.description: pause (no drain): no dispatch rounds may fire while the daemon is paused.

drain_waits_current.description: pause --drain: the current run finishes before dispatch pauses.

next_story_parked.description: pause --drain: the next story must not dispatch while paused.

canceled_terminal_event.description: cancel: a run.canceled terminal event must land.

same_run_id_resumes.description: fail --force: resume must reuse the SAME run id.

recovery_within_dispatch_intervals.description: restart_daemon: all in-flight runs recover within this many dispatch intervals.

token_flush_preserved.description: restart_daemon: the token flush is preserved across the daemon restart.

type.description: Injection kind. sigstop_sigcont: SIGSTOP the target process, hold, then SIGCONT. kill-harness: send a signal (default SIGKILL) to the active harness process for the run. kill-daemon: send a signal (default SIGKILL) to the TT daemon (never the production daemon). delete-tstx-row: delete the TSTX evidence row(s) matching the declared tree hash. move-branch (US-004, S29 premise redesign): move the case's TARGET REF in the worktree-origin repository (the provisioned work clone) to its parent commit — the colleague target-move injection that makes merge.target_moved / reroute exhaustion genuinely fire; ref names the target ref (e.g. refs/heads/main), repeat the number of persistent moves (default 1), interval_s the seconds between repeated moves (REQUIRED when repeat > 1; with rearm a minimum-spacing floor), wait_timeout_s the per-phase-marker wait bound in seconds (default 120; the controller passes it to tt-chaos as --timeout), rearm (US-007 S36) the per-attempt re-arm mode (each fresh step:<role>:running occurrence triggers the next move after rearm_hold_s), rearm_hold_s the post-marker hold in seconds (REQUIRED when rearm: true).

target.description: Process/data class the injection targets. Per-type: sigstop_sigcont and kill-harness target harness_process; kill-daemon targets daemon_process; delete-tstx-row targets tstx_row; move-branch targets origin_target_ref (the case's target branch ref inside the provisioned worktree-origin repository).

trigger.description: Phase marker that arms the injection (e.g. mid_round).

hold_seconds.description: SIGSTOP hold duration in seconds before SIGCONT. REQUIRED ONLY for sigstop_sigcont (per-type constraint enforced by the controller's semantic validator); must be ABSENT for kill-harness/kill-daemon/delete-tstx-row.

signal.description: OPTIONAL signal for kill actions (kill-harness/kill-daemon); defaults to SIGKILL. Must be ABSENT for sigstop_sigcont/delete-tstx-row.

tree.description: Tree hash whose TSTX evidence rows delete-tstx-row deletes. REQUIRED for delete-tstx-row (per-type constraint enforced by the controller's semantic validator); must be ABSENT for other types.

ref.description: Target ref in the worktree-origin repository that move-branch moves (e.g. refs/heads/main). REQUIRED for move-branch (per-type constraint enforced by the controller's semantic validator); must be ABSENT for other types.

repeat.description: move-branch only: number of persistent target moves (default 1). repeat > 1 requires interval_s — each move after the first lands interval_s seconds later, spreading the target pressure across the run's finalize window so the merger's expected-tip check observes a moved tip.

interval_s.description: move-branch only: seconds between repeated moves. REQUIRED when repeat > 1 (per-type constraint enforced by the controller's semantic validator); must be ABSENT when repeat is absent or 1. With rearm: true this is a MINIMUM-SPACING FLOOR (never a free-running cadence) — moves are never fired closer together than interval_s, but each move is triggered by a fresh step:<role>:running occurrence.

rearm.description: move-branch only (US-007 S36 premise redesign): per-attempt re-arm mode. With rearm: true the loop is NOT a free-running clock — each FRESH step:<role>:running occurrence (the step transitions waiting->pending->running on every reroute cycle) triggers the next move after the rearm_hold_s post-marker hold, so EVERY finalize attempt observes a moved tip (the S36 fix: a free-running cadence only landed a move inside a finalize window when the window straddled the next tick). Requires a step: trigger and repeat > 1; must be ABSENT for other types and when repeat is 1.

rearm_hold_s.description: move-branch only (US-007 S36): the post-marker hold in seconds before each re-armed move — long enough for the merger's tip capture to precede the move (2-5s). REQUIRED when rearm: true; must be ABSENT otherwise.

wait_timeout_s.description: OPTIONAL bound (seconds) for each tt-chaos phase-marker wait (the initial trigger arming and, with repeat, the run-terminal stop check cadence). Passed to tt-chaos as --timeout. Defaults to tt-chaos's 120s when absent. Long-injection cells (S29 premise redesign: a trigger minutes into the run) MUST declare it or the operator exits 2 TRIGGER_NEVER before the trigger fires.

operator.description: Executable that performs the injection: bin/tt-chaos.

run_id.description: Scripted run id the ledger row declares. A placeholder (null or empty) is filled by the controller with the ACTUAL launch run id at oracle-evaluation time (T2.1 US-010).

expected_tokens.description: Attributed token sum the scripted run must equal (0 for zero-token scripted cells).

synthetic_token_ledger.description: O11 synthetic-token ledger declaration for scripted WORKFLOW runs (T2.1 US-010): one row per run, run_id filled by the controller. May accompany a typed injection block or stand alone (declaration-only).
